method: Direct finite semantic expansion of the closed DAG only; no claim about omitted runtime/environment behavior.

cases.falsification_value: The checker distinguishes a supported but false invariant from a passing certificate.
The checker refuses an out-of-language operation instead of silently approximating it.

scope: This closes only exact finite integer/bool DAG assertions in bounded-int-dataflow-v1. It cannot compile code, execute loops, inspect files/processes/network, resolve dependencies, measure time, use randomness, or model external effects. Any such request is UNSUPPORTED rather than parity-complete.

design_revision.before: Static substitutes were hand-written predicates tied to individual artifacts.
design_revision.after: A versioned proof-carrying finite DAG now separates reusable exact semantics (PASS/FAIL) from explicit capability refusal (UNSUPPORTED), allowing more small arithmetic/state-transition checks without pretending to provide arbitrary execution.

next_test: Add an independent malformed/overflow control and then test stale COMPACT_HEAD boundary recovery; do not expand the language unless the new operation has equally exact bounded semantics.
